To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
energy dissipation and chemical treatment (polyacrylamide) can improve the performance of stilling basings for treating turbid waters, but that energy dissipation alone is ineffective.
The addition of polyacrylic amide (PAM), an anionic polymer, to the water entering the stilling basin reduced turbidity and T.S.S by up to 88 and 84 percent, respectively.
The use of energy dissipaters and polyacrylamides can improve turbidity and sediment removal efficiency in permanent pool stilling basins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach to the study of the effect of the turbidity on the performance of the water.
the development of an innovative technology for the removal of suspended sediment and turbidity from water.
the development of a new approach to improve the performance of stilling basings for treating turbid surface water.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of energy dissipaters with PAM treatment can reduce turbidity and TTS in a stilling basin by up to 90% and 85%, respectively.

the addition of PAM to the stilling basins, with or without the addition of energy dissipation treatments, is a very effective way of reducing turbidity and suspended solids in water from construction sites.
the addition of PAM to a stilling basin with or without energy dissipaters is a very effective way to reduce turbidity and suspended solids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the addition of PAM was more important than the physical energy dissipators for reducing turbidity and suspended solids, but the physical treatments were important for improving the effectiveness of the PAM treatment by reducing floc break up.
PAM is the key treatment for reducing turbidity and suspended solids.

the addition of a chemical treatment (PAM) to the stilling basins was more effective at removing turbidity and TSO than the physical treatments (BILS, coir baffles, and Pyramat) and that the coir and Pyramat materials were more effective at trapping sediment than BILS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of energy dissipators and a chemical flocculant can significantly improve the performance of stilling bas-ins for treating turbid waters, and that a simple baffle is adequate.
the addition of PAM is the primary factor in reducing turbidity and sediment in a stilling basin.
the addition of PAM is more important than physical treatments for removing turbidity and TTS from pumped water.
